To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The majority of faecal E. coli strains in 16 calves changed over time.
there was a continual turn-over in E. coli strains and that the incidence of antibiotic resistance changed markedly with the calves' age.

the strains of E. coli colonizing the calves changed continually, that antibiotic resistant strains were isolated from calves in the first weeks after birth, and that the incidence of resistance declined as the calves grew older.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of the ecology of the intestinal tract of the young calf, with special reference to the factors affecting the colonization of the gut with Escherichia. coli.
the ecology of Eschericia coli in dairy calves.
the epidemiological aspects of Escherichiia coli infection in calves and the factors that may be responsible for the continual change in the composition of the faecal E. coli flora.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the E. coli population of calves reared as replacements for dairy cows is in a continual state of flux and that the strains colonizing the calves at any one time can be expected to change with the age of animal.
the calves were exposed to E. coli strains which had a high ARI, but that the calves' resistance to the strains was such that the ARI fell to low levels as the calves aged.
E. coli strains are continually changing in calves and the ARI is a useful indicator of this change.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the calves were initially exposed to E. coli strains of low resistance to antimicrobial agents, which may have been present in their dam's udder, but were subsequently exposed to a large number of resistant strains, which were probably present in the environment.
the majority of the strains of E. coli in calves rearing as dairy cow replacements are continually changing and this is associated with a continual change in the ARI of these isolates.
the majority of the E. coli strains colonizing calves in the early stages of life were sensitive to antibiotics but that the calves were exposed to a large number of antibiotic resistant strains.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ARI can be used to assess the impact of management changes on the E. coli flora of calves.
the calves were continually being colonized by different strains and the strains which colonized the calves were not the same strains as were isolated from their dams.
the E. coli flora of calves is in a continual state of flux.
